subtopics.title: From Open Pits to Underground Mines

questions.question: Why did the Kimberley mines move underground in the 1880s?
options: The diamonds had run out at the surface
Reef falls, flooding and great depth made open-pit mining impossible

questions.question: Blue ground is:
options: The diamond-bearing rock of the volcanic pipe

questions.question: Why did underground mining favour large companies?
options: It was cheaper than open-pit mining
It needed expensive engines, pumps, rails and explosives

questions.question: Why did the gold mines of the Witwatersrand become very deep?
options: The mines had to avoid the diamond pipes
Gold is only found at the centre of the earth
The gold reefs were thin layers sloping deep into the earth

questions.question: What was the most common cause of death underground?
A misfire was:
options: A fire in the compound kitchen
A dynamite charge that did not explode and could later be struck by a drill

questions.question: The De Beers Mine fire of 1888 killed about:
options: 200 miners, most of them black workers

questions.question: Why was the air in deep mines hot?
options: The temperature of the rock rises with depth
The sun shines into the tunnels
Workers lit fires for cooking underground

subtopics.title: Disease, the Colour Bar and Unequal Treatment

questions.question: Silicosis was caused by:
options: Poor diet with no vitamin C

questions.question: Scurvy is caused by:
The colour bar meant that:
options: All workers were paid the same
Certain skilled and supervisory jobs were reserved for white workers

questions.question: Which law later gave legal force to the colour bar on the mines?
options: The Mines and Works Act of 1911

subtopics.title: Sources, Calculations and the Error Museum

questions.question: A mine employs 4 000 workers and 120 die in a year. What is the death rate per 1 000 workers?
Which is a limit of company records as a source?
options: They rarely include the voices of workers

questions.question: Which statement belongs in the error museum?
options: The Kimberley mines were always underground
Rockfalls were the most common cause of death
The De Beers fire killed mainly black workers

questions.question: How did some workers resist dangerous conditions?
options: By buying shares in the mines
By avoiding mines with bad reputations and refusing dangerous work

questions.question: From about which year did Kimberley companies begin underground mining?
Where were the shafts sunk?
options: In the middle of the compound
Outside the pit, in solid rock

questions.question: Who could afford underground mining?
What did miners use to drill holes for dynamite in the early years?
options: Hammers and steel drills, by hand

questions.question: Shifts underground were often:
Lashing meant:
Who mainly did the heavy manual work underground?
Compared with black workers, white workers:
options: Earned less and lived in compounds
Earned many times more and could form trade unions

questions.question: Pneumonia was a major killer partly because workers:
options: Came up from hot, damp mines into cold nights
